memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal is to be put to death." - Exodus 22:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard verse to read, and we should not rush past it. God draws an absolute line here, and the severity of the penalty reflects how profoundly such an act violates the created order He established. From the beginning, God designed intimacy within clear and good boundaries. To shatter those boundaries so completely was, in Israel's context, treated as a grave corruption that could not be allowed to spread.

While we do not live under Israel's civil penalties today, the underlying truth stands firm: God's design for human dignity and intimacy is not arbitrary. His boundaries flow from His wisdom and His care for us. When we honour the order He built into creation, we flourish; when we tear it apart, we bring ruin on ourselves and others. His commands, even the severe ones, are the guardrails of a loving Father.

At its heart, this verse reminds us that human beings are made in God's image, set apart with a unique dignity. We are not meant to live as though we were merely animals driven by every impulse. In Christ, we are called upward — to holiness, to self-control, to a life that honours the Maker's design (1 Thess 4:7). God's boundaries are never meant to diminish us but to guard the dignity He has given us. We can trust the wisdom behind every line He draws.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust that God's boundaries flow from His wisdom and care for me?
Where do I need to honour God's design rather than following every impulse?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have made me in Your image with unique dignity. Help me trust the wisdom behind Your boundaries and live in the holiness to which You call me. Amen.
